v.q: A `@Transactional` service method throws a checked `IOException` and nothing else is configured. What happens to the transaction?
o: It commits, as only unchecked exceptions and errors roll back
It rolls back, because any exception rolls back
It rolls back only if the exception is in `throws`
It stays open until the caller decides
v.w: By default Spring rolls back on RuntimeException and Error only. Use `rollbackFor = Exception.class` to include checked exceptions.

v.q: Which exception rolls back a @Transactional method by default?
v.w: Unchecked exceptions and errors roll back. Use rollbackFor for checked ones.

v.q: `transfer()` is `@Transactional` and calls `this.audit()` in the same class. `audit()` is `@Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW)`. What happens?
o: `audit()` joins the same transaction, as the call skips the proxy
`audit()` starts a new, independent transaction as annotated
Spring throws an exception about the annotation at startup
`audit()` runs with no transaction at all, not even a joined one
v.w: The transaction advice lives in a proxy. A call on `this` is a plain method call, so the annotation on the inner method is ignored. Move it to another bean.

v.q: Which call from outside the bean starts the REQUIRES_NEW transaction?
v.w: The call must pass through the proxy.

v.q: An outer `REQUIRED` method catches a `RuntimeException` thrown by an inner `REQUIRED` method and returns normally. What does the commit do?
o: It fails with `UnexpectedRollbackException`: the transaction is rollback-only
It succeeds and saves all of the work done by the outer method
It succeeds but silently skips only the work of the inner method
It retries the inner method once and then commits the result
v.w: REQUIRED joins one physical transaction. The inner failure marks it rollback-only, and catching the exception does not clear that mark.

v.q: Which situation leaves an outer transaction rollback-only?
o: An inner REQUIRED method throws and the outer catches it
The outer method returns normally with no errors
v.w: Both share one transaction. The inner failure marked it rollback-only.

v.q: Which propagation suits an audit record that must be saved even if the main business transaction rolls back?
v.w: REQUIRES_NEW suspends the outer transaction and commits independently on its own connection.

v.q: Which propagation joins an existing transaction or starts one?
You publish a message to a broker inside a `@Transactional` method just before it returns. What is the main risk?
o: The consumer may act before commit, or the transaction may roll back
The broker rejects any message that is sent inside a transaction
The message is always delivered twice by the broker
The transaction cannot commit while a message is being sent
v.w: Use `@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)` for simple cases or the transactional outbox for guaranteed delivery.

v.q: Which pattern keeps database changes and published messages consistent?
v.w: The event is stored with the data and published after the commit.

v.q: Why is calling a slow remote service inside a transaction a problem?
o: It holds a pooled connection and locks, so slow calls exhaust the pool
Remote calls are simply not allowed inside any transaction
The remote call is rolled back automatically by Spring
It turns the whole transaction into a read-only one
v.w: Keep transactions short: no remote calls, file I/O or waiting inside them.

v.q: Which statement about long transactions is NOT true?
o: A remote call inside a transaction is free
v.w: Slow calls keep resources locked while they wait.

v.q: A method annotated `@Async` and `@Transactional` is called from another bean. In which transaction does the async body run?
o: In its own new transaction on the async thread
In one transaction shared by all async threads
v.w: The transaction is bound to a thread. The caller's transaction does not follow the work onto another thread.

v.q: In which transaction does a @Transactional @Async method run when called from another bean?
o: One shared by all async calls
v.w: Transactions are bound to threads, so the context does not move.

Any attempt to write always throws an exception right away
The method runs without any transaction being started
The transaction is run with SERIALIZABLE isolation instead
v.w: readOnly is an optimisation hint, not a security or integrity mechanism.

v.q: What does readOnly = true actually give you?
v.w: It may skip dirty checking, but it is not a security feature.
